text:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — GPU pool 'rg-gpu-pool' high queue depth + HPA metrics delay detected. 90th latency up 4x, autoscaler not spawning new pods (external metrics stale)
ops-bot: polling k8s and metrics endpoints now
alex (oncall): ack, I'm on it. Paging eng-runtime and eng-infra. Any customer-facing impact?
carol (support): Getting reports from FinSaaS and EduScale about 429s and timed requests since ~10:02 UTC. Ticket spikes in last 10m.
priya (eng-runtime): seeing sustained request queue growth on inference-service shards. Pod CPU low, GPU util near 98%, but HPA external metric (prom-adapter) shows zeros for last 3m. suspect metrics adapter backlog.
dmitri (eng-infra): prometheus-adapter logs show backlog and 503s to prometheus; metrics-server OOM restarted twice in 8m. Could be a spike of scrape cardinality.
lia (eng-sre): summary from dashboards: queue length +420% in 6m, Pod Throttle rate high, service errors (429/503) at ~15% traffic. Customers on dedicated pools affected first.
alex (oncall): immediate mitigations? priya / dmitri, suggestions?
priya (eng-runtime): try disabling external metrics fallback limit so HPA can read node metrics. Also restart prom-adapter to clear its internal queue.
priya (eng-runtime): commands I will run:```bash
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/prometheus-adapter
kubectl -n kube-system scale deployment/metrics-server --replicas=3
kubectl -n inference scale deployment/rg-gpu-pool --replicas=8
```
ops-bot: noted change plan. Will run once we confirm no risk to ongoing jobs.
dmitri (eng-infra): I'll bump GPU nodepool autoscaling lower threshold and add 2 nodes manually to buy time. Running:```bash
gcloud container node-pools update gpu-pool --cluster=prod --enable-autoscaling --min-nodes=4 --max-nodes=50
gcloud compute instances create gpu-emergency-1 --machine-type=n1-highmem-8 --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-t4,count=1
```
priya (eng-runtime): restarting prom-adapter now — doing a graceful restart to avoid dropping metrics abruptly.
pagerduty-bot: alex (oncall) acknowledged the page at 10:05:45 UTC
priya (eng-runtime): prom-adapter restart completed, logs show metric backlog flush starting. Observed external-metrics endpoint returning values again.
lia (eng-sre): metrics-server scaled to 3 pods, memory pressure reduced. No more OOMs in last 30s.
dmitri (eng-infra): manual node additions booting, kubelet registering new nodes.
carol (support): FinSaaS confirms reduced errors on some routes, still seeing throttling for long-running batches. Communicating mitigation to customers. :white_check_mark:
alex (oncall): I'm going to open a short-lived routing rule: divert low-priority batch traffic to best-effort queue to relieve main pool. Lia, can you apply traffic shaping?
lia (eng-sre): applying a temporary policy in envoy route table to add header x-traffic-class=low for batch endpoints. Will also throttle concurrency via ingress.```yaml
# envoy tweak
- match: /v1/batch
  route: best-effort
  rate_limit: 10rps
```
priya (eng-runtime): autoscaler now reading external metrics again. HPA has triggered 3 additional replicas for inference service, but they are pending GPU assignment — node additions should resolve it.
ops-bot: observed queue length dropping from peak 900 -> 320 in 2m after restarts and manual scale.
alex (oncall): customer impact assessment: two enterprise customers experienced increased error rates and higher latencies between 10:02–10:12 UTC. No data leakage. Estimated affected p99 latency increase 2.3x, error budget consumed for FinSaaS route ~12%.
carol (support): logged CSAT hits and created priority incidents for FinSaaS and EduScale, assigned to AE leads. Notifying customers about mitigation steps + ETA for full recovery.
dmitri (eng-infra): nodes ready and pods scheduling to new GPUs. GPU utilization balancing across pods now ~72%.
priya (eng-runtime): HPA stabilized and is respecting target utilization again. I'll put prom-adapter under enhanced logging for 12h and add a backpressure metric to alert earlier.
lia (eng-sre): created an incident timeline and initial RCA notes. Suspected root cause: sudden scrape cardinality spike in prometheus (new debug labels rolled out) caused prom-adapter to fall behind, metrics-server OOMed under memory pressure, external metrics stale -> HPA didn't scale quickly -> queue growth -> GPU pool exhausted.
alex (oncall): handoff in 30m to oncall-next, will include checklist: restart prom-adapter, verify metrics-server stability, confirm HPA external metrics, scale nodepool if queue > 400 for >5m, communicate to customers.
customer-success-bot: Notifying Customer Success on handoff: cs-team@redwood, incident notes saved to /incidents/1779998765.
lia (eng-sre): postmortem actions created: 1) revert debug label rollout that spiked cardinality, 2) add rate-limits for debug label values, 3) increase prom-adapter queue capacity and metrics-server memory request, 4) set an early alert for prom-adapter backlog > 200k.
alex (oncall): marking mitigations as complete for now. Will monitor for 1h then close page if stable. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
ops-bot: monitoring rule: queue-length dropped to 120 and error rate down to 1.2% at 10:15:05 UTC
carol (support): customers updated. No immediate escalations.
priya (eng-runtime): follow-up: I'll prepare a PR to add backpressure instrumenting to the adapter and an autoscale-fallback to node-level metrics when external metrics stale for >60s.
lia (eng-sre): handing off to oncall-next @sam at 10:35 UTC — transferring timeline & commands.
pagerduty-bot: incident acknowledged by sam (oncall-next) at 10:35:12 UTC
alex (oncall): final note before handoff: consider spike-detection alerting for cardinality changes on prometheus. Good job team, thanks. :clap:
